Related Article Eyal Weizman on Forensic Architecture: ''Mapping is Power''

Reconstructing Architecture Through Sound

For years, independent investigators could study Saydnaya Prison from the outside, including through satellite imagery, but had no access to its interior. Inside the military prison north of Damascus, much of what could be reconstructed depended on the memories of people who had been held there.

For years, independent investigators could study Saydnaya Prison from the outside, including through satellite imagery, but had no access to its interior. Inside the military prison north of Damascus, much of what could be reconstructed depended on the memories of people who had been held there.

In 2016, Forensic Architecture worked with Amnesty International to reconstruct the prison from the memories of five former detainees interviewed in Istanbul. Starting with a rough model based on satellite images and earlier written testimony, researchers developed the interior as survivors described cells, stairwells, and doors. The witnesses explored the rooms at eye level, corrected their proportions, and placed objects where they remembered them. Moving through the model sometimes brought back details they had never mentioned.

In 2016, Forensic Architecture worked with Amnesty International to reconstruct the prison from the memories of five former detainees interviewed in Istanbul. Starting with a rough model based on satellite images and earlier written testimony, researchers developed the interior as survivors described cells, stairwells, and doors. The witnesses explored the rooms at eye level, corrected their proportions, and placed objects where they remembered them. Moving through the model sometimes brought back details they had never mentioned.

Some dimensions came from physical memories of the building. One survivor remembered the size of a hatch in his cell door because guards had forced him to push his head through it. Another estimated the dimensions of a cell by counting its floor tiles.

Some dimensions came from physical memories of the building. One survivor remembered the size of a hatch in his cell door because guards had forced him to push his head through it. Another estimated the dimensions of a cell by counting its floor tiles.

Sound provided another way to reconstruct the interior. Detainees were frequently blindfolded or kept in darkness, and speaking was prohibited. They became attentive to footsteps, doors, and noises traveling through water pipes and ventilation ducts. Audio investigator Lawrence Abu Hamdan gathered what the team called "ear-witness testimony," using simulated echoes and reverberations to help survivors recall the spaces they had occupied. These comparisons helped estimate the dimensions of cells, corridors, and stairwells.

Sound provided another way to reconstruct the interior. Detainees were frequently blindfolded or kept in darkness, and speaking was prohibited. They became attentive to footsteps, doors, and noises traveling through water pipes and ventilation ducts. Audio investigator Lawrence Abu Hamdan gathered what the team called "ear-witness testimony," using simulated echoes and reverberations to help survivors recall the spaces they had occupied. These comparisons helped estimate the dimensions of cells, corridors, and stairwells.

The investigation also documented how sound traveled through the prison's architecture. Pipes and ventilation ducts carried noises between spaces, while differences in echoes and reverberation helped survivors distinguish rooms and corridors they could rarely see. In his related work, Saydnaya (the missing 19dB), Abu Hamdan examined how enforced silence had intensified after 2011, including a 19-decibel reduction in the whispering levels remembered by survivors.

In his related work, Saydnaya (the missing 19dB), Abu Hamdan examined how enforced silence had intensified after 2011, including a 19-decibel reduction in the whispering levels remembered by survivors.

The accounts did not always agree. Witnesses had experienced Saydnaya under different conditions, so the team cross-referenced spatial and acoustic testimony, corrected discrepancies where possible, and documented those that remained. These differences could also reveal how individual prisoners had experienced and remembered the building. The resulting interactive model can be explored by location or by witness, bringing their accounts together within one reconstructed space.

These differences could also reveal how individual prisoners had experienced and remembered the building. The resulting interactive model can be explored by location or by witness, bringing their accounts together within one reconstructed space.

The relationship between the model and the building changed in December 2024, when the fall of the Assad government made Saydnaya accessible to journalists, families, and investigators. Its interior could finally be examined directly, opening the possibility of comparing the reconstruction with the prison's physical dimensions. Yet the survivors' testimonies also preserved information about how they had experienced those spaces through darkness, sound, and enforced silence, details that a physical survey alone could not recover.

At Saydnaya, different recollections helped reconstruct the same building. In Famagusta, Cyprus, entire communities had developed different understandings of the same city.

At Saydnaya, different recollections helped reconstruct the same building. In Famagusta, Cyprus, entire communities had developed different understandings of the same city.

The 1974 conflict displaced much of Famagusta's Greek Cypriot population and left Varosha, a coastal district, under Turkish military control. Former residents retained memories of neighborhoods they could no longer enter, while those who remained or arrived later experienced a city shaped by territorial divisions. Both groups knew the city, but their memories described different urban landscapes.

Former residents retained memories of neighborhoods they could no longer enter, while those who remained or arrived later experienced a city shaped by territorial divisions. Both groups knew the city, but their memories described different urban landscapes.

Led by architect and urbanist Socrates Stratis, Hands-on Famagusta explored these divided perceptions through what the team described as split mental maps. The project developed a series of counter-mapping tools, including large isometric drawings, an interactive digital platform, and a transportable physical model. These representations were used in workshops, public presentations, and discussions involving participants from across the Cypriot divide.

Led by architect and urbanist Socrates Stratis, Hands-on Famagusta explored these divided perceptions through what the team described as split mental maps. The project developed a series of counter-mapping tools, including large isometric drawings, an interactive digital platform, and a transportable physical model. These representations were used in workshops, public presentations, and discussions involving participants from across the Cypriot divide.

The drawings made the city's territorial fragmentation visible, documenting enclaves, restricted areas, and the boundaries separating different parts of Famagusta. The physical model presented a different spatial condition. By representing built areas, open landscapes, and neighborhoods as one continuous territory, it allowed participants to examine relationships between places that had become difficult to experience together. Areas separated by political boundaries could be viewed within the same urban composition, revealing connections that were absent from the communities' everyday experience of the city.

This shared representation became a reference for discussing Famagusta's possible futures. Participants could examine the same streets, neighborhoods, and open spaces while approaching them through different memories and territorial experiences. Stratis and Emre Akbil describe this approach through dissensus, recognizing disagreement as part of collective urban discussion. The project's counter-mapping tools were later presented through Contested Fronts, the Cyprus Pavilion at the 2016 Venice Architecture Biennale, demonstrating how architectural representation could provide a common spatial reference for communities whose understanding of the city remained divided.

Tracing Disappeared Architecture at Full Scale

Barcelona presents a different condition. On the site of the city's former municipal courts, historical records preserve the outlines of buildings that have disappeared, even as their dimensions are no longer visible on the ground.

Barcelona presents a different condition. On the site of the city's former municipal courts, historical records preserve the outlines of buildings that have disappeared, even as their dimensions are no longer visible on the ground.

For the 2022 Model Barcelona Architectures Festival, FLEXOARQUITECTURA developed Memoria Cronotópica, an installation that transferred historical architectural drawings directly onto the site at a scale of 1:1. Using different colors to distinguish periods, the architects traced the footprints of former structures across the ground, allowing visitors to encounter their original dimensions through movement.

For the 2022 Model Barcelona Architectures Festival, FLEXOARQUITECTURA developed Memoria Cronotópica, an installation that transferred historical architectural drawings directly onto the site at a scale of 1:1. Using different colors to distinguish periods, the architects traced the footprints of former structures across the ground, allowing visitors to encounter their original dimensions through movement.

The drawings brought together several centuries of occupation. Beneath the former courthouse lay a medieval necropolis with sixteen burials dating from the 7th to 9th centuries. The site had also accommodated the Fusina Gardens and the Palau de Belles Arts, an exhibition building constructed for the 1888 Universal Exposition. By superimposing the outlines of these different occupations onto the same surface, the installation made their dimensions and spatial relationships visible simultaneously. Visitors could move between the footprints of structures that had occupied the site at different moments, comparing their scales and positions against the surrounding urban fabric.

Two temporary towers marked the original positions of the Palau de Belles Arts' organs. During the festival, musician Juan de la Rubia performed an organ piece, briefly bringing a sound associated with the demolished building back to the site. Alongside the ground drawings, the performance introduced another way of recalling an architectural space that no longer existed.

The historical drawings, however, recorded only certain moments of the site's development. After the courthouse was demolished, the vacant plot accumulated demolition aggregate, while plants and animals began to occupy the space. By placing historical outlines over these emerging conditions, FLEXOARQUITECTURA also raised questions about the site's future: whether former buildings could have been adapted, their materials reused, or temporary uses introduced alongside the ecosystem that had begun to develop.

By placing historical outlines over these emerging conditions, FLEXOARQUITECTURA also raised questions about the site's future: whether former buildings could have been adapted, their materials reused, or temporary uses introduced alongside the ecosystem that had begun to develop.

Architectural drawings preserve dimensions and spatial relationships, but the experience of a place is harder to document. A room can be measured through its walls, openings, and circulation, while its proportions may also be remembered through sound and movement. A city can be mapped as a continuous territory, even when political boundaries divide how its inhabitants experience it. A demolished building can survive in historical plans while its scale disappears from the ground. Each form of representation captures particular aspects of a place while leaving others undocumented.

These projects reveal how much depends on the sources used to produce a representation. Testimonies may contradict one another, communities may disagree about the territory they share, and historical archives preserve only certain moments of a site's development. Deciding how to work with those differences becomes part of the architectural process. What enters the drawing, and what remains outside it, depends on whose knowledge is used to construct it.

#8986. Hyatt Category 4 Free Night Certificate — Card Perk Sweet Spot

Savings rate, FI number, and the path to freedom.

Withdrawal plans, Roth ladders, and early access.

Index funds, asset allocation, and real estate.

Roth conversions, capital gains, and FI tax planning.

Career growth, side hustles, and entrepreneurship.

Beliefs, purpose, and financial psychology.

Exercise, nutrition, and mental wellness.

The simplest high-value card perk in travel rewards — no points math required

Picture this: you walk into a stunning hotel lobby — maybe it's the Hyatt Regency Kyoto, maybe it's the Andaz Maui at Wailea, maybe it's a chic Hyatt Centric in the heart of a city you've always wanted to explore. You hand over your World of Hyatt card at check-in, and the night is on the house. Not because you're a high roller. Not because you spent $50,000 on a credit card. Because you crossed a spending threshold you were hitting anyway, and Hyatt rewarded you with a free night certificate that covers any Category 1–4 property in the entire portfolio. This is what the ChooseFI community means when we talk about travel rewards done right: identifying the moments where a credit card benefit perfectly intersects with your normal life, and extracting maximum value with minimum complexity. ## The Math That Makes This a No-Brainer Here's the value proposition in plain numbers. Category 4 Hyatt properties — places like the Thompson Nashville, the Hyatt Regency Maui, or the Andaz San Diego — regularly command **$200 to $400 per night** in cash. On peak dates, holiday weekends, or in premium markets, that number climbs even higher. Your free night certificate covers any of these properties at no additional points cost. None. Zero. This isn't a discount. It's a full, unrestricted free night at properties that charge real-world luxury rates. Why does this represent a genuine pricing inefficiency? Because Hyatt's Category 1–4 certificates are earned through a flat spending threshold — $15,000 on the World of Hyatt Credit Card in a calendar year — and can be redeemed at properties whose nightly rates vary enormously. A Category 4 certificate costs the same to earn whether you use it at a $150 roadside property or a $400 resort. The system rewards you for targeting the high end of the range every single time. For a household already putting everyday spending on a rewards card, $15,000 across a full calendar year is often an achievable benchmark. Groceries, utilities, insurance premiums, quarterly tax payments — it adds up faster than you think. And when it does, Hyatt drops a certificate in your account that can deliver **$300–$400 in hotel value** without spending a single additional point. In the World of Hyatt program — consistently rated the **best hotel loyalty program for value per point** — this certificate is one of the most quietly powerful perks on any hotel card in the market.

The core mechanism here isn't a transfer partnership exploit or a routing rule loophole. It's simpler and more durable than that: Hyatt's Category system creates a ceiling, not a floor. When you earn a Category 1–4 free night certificate, you're not locked into a $150-a-night budget motel. You're handed a key that opens any door in that range — and some of those doors lead to genuinely spectacular properties.

Hyatt operates on a fixed award chart, ranging from 3,500 points for a Category 1 night all the way up to 45,000 points for a Category 8 night. Unlike programs that use dynamic pricing (where award costs swing with cash demand), Hyatt's chart is static. A Category 4 property costs the same 15,000 points whether it's a Tuesday in February or New Year's Eve.

Your free night certificate functions exactly like those 15,000 points — but you earned it through card spending, not through a points balance. This means the certificate has a defined and predictable value: whatever a Category 4 property charges in cash on the night you use it is exactly what you're getting for free.

The pricing inefficiency exists because Hyatt assigns categories based on average nightly rates across the year — but peak-season rates at desirable Category 4 properties can blow well past that average. A Hyatt Regency in a major city might be Category 4 because its average annual rate qualifies, but on a conference weekend or holiday weekend, that same room might cost $350–$400. Your certificate captures that peak-season value without any upcharge.

While this sweet spot is certificate-based (no points required), World of Hyatt integrates beautifully with two major transferable currency programs:

This matters for your broader strategy. If you want to stack a certificate with a separate points redemption — say, booking multiple nights where the first is covered by the certificate and subsequent nights use transferred points — you have two strong, flexible on-ramps into the Hyatt ecosystem. Chase Ultimate Rewards is the workhorse of the FI community's travel rewards stack, and having Hyatt as an instant 1:1 partner makes it one of the most actionable transfer relationships in the game.

Hyatt charges no fuel surcharges on award redemptions — a meaningful distinction compared to some airline programs where surcharges can swallow most of your savings. Your certificate redemption is clean: one certificate, one free night, no surprise fees at checkout beyond standard resort fees (which, to be fair, do apply at some properties — more on that in Pro Tips).

World of Hyatt points expire after 24 months of account inactivity. As a World of Hyatt Credit Card holder, your card activity will naturally keep your account active, so expiry is rarely a concern for cardholders. But if you ever cancel the card, make sure you use your points and certificates before they age out.

Booking a World of Hyatt free night certificate is genuinely one of the easiest processes in all of travel rewards. Here's the complete walkthrough from certificate to check-in.

Log in to your World of Hyatt account at hyatt.com and navigate to your account dashboard. Under the "My Certificates & Awards" section, confirm your Category 1–4 free night certificate is present and note its expiration date. Certificates are typically valid for 12 months from issuance, so don't let it sit unused. If you don't see it and you've crossed the $15,000 annual spend threshold on your World of Hyatt Credit Card, allow a few days for it to post after your statement closes, or call Chase to confirm.

Go to hyatt.com and use the hotel search function. You can filter by World of Hyatt category — specifically, search for Category 4 properties in any destination you're targeting. Don't shortchange yourself by defaulting to a Category 1 or 2 property out of habit. The certificate works at any Category 1–4 property, so always target the top of the range. Look for properties with high nightly cash rates — this is where your certificate delivers the most value.

Once you've identified a target property, search your dates on hyatt.com and switch the search to "Use Points." Category 4 properties will show award availability for 15,000 points per night. If award availability shows for that date, your certificate will cover it. Hyatt's booking window opens 395 days in advance, so for peak travel dates — holidays, major events, popular travel seasons — you can and should book the maximum window out.

Proceed through the booking process. At the payment step, you'll see an option to "Apply Free Night Award" or select your certificate from your account. Select the Category 1–4 certificate. The system will apply it and your total cash charge drops to $0 for the room rate (plus taxes and any applicable resort fees).

Hyatt award availability at popular properties can be limited during peak periods. Your tactical options:

Hyatt operates on a fixed category system where each property is assigned a category from 1 to 8 based on the brand and location, not the current market rate. This creates a structural pricing inefficiency: a Category 4 property in a high-demand market like Maui or Kyoto charges the same certificate cost as a Category 4 in a mid-tier city. Your free night certificate works at all of them equally. Unlike hotel programs with dynamic pricing where the cost of a free night fluctuates with demand, Hyatt's fixed chart means you can target the highest-value Category 4 properties without paying more. The card's $95 annual fee is one of the lowest in the premium hotel card category, yet the certificate alone delivers $250 to $400 or more in value — a return that makes the math trivially easy for any FI-minded household.

Let's make this concrete with a real example that represents exactly how this certificate shines.

The Andaz San Diego is a boutique lifestyle hotel in the Gaslamp Quarter — rooftop pool, stylish rooms, walking distance to everything downtown. During Comic-Con, a Padres playoff weekend, or a major convention, rates push past $400.

Cash cost: $300 (conservative weekend estimate) Certificate cost: 0 points, 1 Category 1–4 free night certificate Your out-of-pocket: $0 for the room rate

You earned this certificate by crossing $15,000 in annual spending on the World of Hyatt Credit Card — a threshold many households reach through regular everyday spending over 12 months. The certificate posts automatically, you search availability on hyatt.com, and you apply it at checkout in about five minutes.

You're not redeeming into a budget experience. The Andaz brand sits at the upper-upscale tier of the Hyatt portfolio. You check in through a host model (no formal front desk), settle into a room with thoughtful design, and wake up knowing that $300 night cost you nothing extra beyond your normal spending.

If you hold World of Hyatt elite status — Discoverist, Explorist, or Globalist — that status applies to certificate bookings exactly like paid stays. Room upgrade requests, early check-in, late check-out: all the same benefits apply.

In every case, your one certificate delivers more value than most points redemptions in any hotel program. And you earned it without touching your points balance.

Your certificate works identically at a $150/night Category 4 property and a $400/night Category 4 property. Always search for the properties with the highest cash rates in your target destination. Use hyatt.com's rate display to compare award availability against current cash pricing — this directly shows you the value you're capturing.

Hyatt's booking window opens 395 days in advance. For properties in high-demand markets — Maui, New York, Chicago during peak season — award inventory gets claimed fast. Set a calendar alert to search exactly 395 days before your target dates and book the moment the window opens.

Your certificate covers one night. If you're staying multiple nights, stack it strategically: apply the certificate to the highest-cost night (often a Saturday) and book the remaining nights with World of Hyatt points transferred instantly from Chase Ultimate Rewards or Bilt Rewards at a 1:1 ratio. This hybrid approach maximizes the value of every currency you're using.

World of Hyatt points expire after 24 months of inactivity. As a cardholder, your spending activity resets this clock automatically. But if you ever pause card use, make a small Hyatt purchase — even a $1 on-property charge — to reset the timer and protect your balance.

Hyatt does not waive resort fees on award and certificate bookings at all properties. Before booking, check whether your target property charges a daily resort fee — these can run $25–$50/night and will appear on your final bill. Factor this into your value calculation, especially at resort properties in Hawaii or Las Vegas.

The $15,000 spend threshold should come from natural household spending, not manufactured purchases. In the FI community, we optimize around spending you're doing anyway — insurance premiums, tax payments, groceries, utilities. If you're buying things you don't need to hit the threshold, you're eroding the value of the certificate.

Certificates issued by Hyatt are typically valid for 12 months. Mark the expiration date in your calendar the moment the certificate posts. An expired certificate is $300+ in value that simply disappears — one of the most painful mistakes in travel rewards.

This sweet spot is built for the everyday FI household that's already spending $15,000 or more annually on a single credit card and wants to redirect that activity toward a meaningful travel benefit. You don't need a large points balance. You don't need to understand transfer partners or award chart math. You earn the certificate by spending, you apply it at checkout, and you get a free night at a genuinely nice hotel.

You need: the World of Hyatt Credit Card, $15,000 in annual card spending, and a World of Hyatt account. No minimum points balance required — this is a card perk, not a points redemption.

If your annual spending is significantly below $15,000 on a single card, this particular mechanism won't trigger. In that case, the World of Hyatt Credit Card still earns Hyatt points on spending and delivers a Category 1–4 certificate on each card anniversary — so it retains value, just through a different path. Also, if you're deeply committed to a non-Hyatt hotel program, the benefit is obviously less useful without a library of Hyatt properties in your regular rotation.

## Rated: Easy (4/5 Beginner Friendly) This is one of the most accessible sweet spots in the entire travel rewards ecosystem, and that's by design. The certificate mechanism removes the two biggest friction points in traditional points redemptions: **finding the right number of points** and **navigating complex transfer timing**. You earn the certificate passively through spending, it posts to your account automatically, and the booking process on hyatt.com is as intuitive as booking any other hotel stay. ## What Makes It Easy - **No transfer required** — the certificate lives in your World of Hyatt account, ready to apply at checkout - **Fixed pricing** — Category 4 is Category 4 everywhere in the world; no dynamic pricing surprises - **Simple availability search** — hyatt.com's award search is clean and straightforward ## The One Genuine Challenge: Availability at Popular Properties The only real friction point is award inventory at high-demand Category 4 properties on desirable dates. Hyatt limits how many award rooms it releases per night, and popular properties in destinations like Hawaii or New York fill quickly. **Three ways to beat this:** 1. Search 395 days in advance when fresh inventory releases 2. Build a shortlist of 3–5 Category 4 properties in your target region so you have backup options 3. Stay flexible on dates — midweek nights almost always have more award availability than weekends If you can approach this with even modest date flexibility, you will find great options. The Hyatt portfolio at Category 4 is large and geographically diverse, and there is almost always a compelling property available somewhere you'd actually want to go. For anyone new to travel rewards, this certificate is the perfect first redemption — low complexity, high reward, and a genuinely memorable hotel stay to show your household what this strategy can deliver.

#8985. Pucker Up! How to Heal Cracked Lip Corners Fast

Follow Greatist on our socials for all things health.

Smiling for selfies should be fun, not painful! If cracked lip corners or angular cheilitis make it hard to smile, eat, or kiss, don’t worry. Check out these tips to heal those cracks quickly. With some care and good habits, you’ll have pain-free, makeout-ready lips in no time. Say goodbye to angular cheilitis and hello to a happier smile!

The first step to healing your cracked lip corners quickly is to lock in any moisture. Reach for a product dermatologists call an occlusive, which creates a protective barrier that prevents your lip corners from getting drier. Vaseline, Aquafor, or CeraVe ointment are common occlusives that will help reduce cracking.

Dab a little coconut oil, olive oil, or fragrance-free moisturizer on the corners of your lips daily after you shower. Make it a daily habit, but don’t go overboard. A little dab will do. Allow your skin’s natural oils to build back up as the cracking fades. Bonus tip: Add the occlusive lip barrier after moisturizing.

Locking in moisture only works if you have enough moisture, so staying hydrated is key! Keep a refillable water bottle with you as your trusty sidekick. Sip on plain water throughout the day, or jazz it up with a splash of cucumber or another non-acidic flavor. Pro tip: Avoid lemon juice, which can irritate and sting sensitive skin.

Bonus: Staying hydrated will help your raw lip corners heal quicker and improve your skin’s overall health.

Have you noticed that moisture is a common theme here? Lend your lips a humid hand by sleeping with a humidifier beside your bed. Adding moisture to the air is especially helpful for your cracked lips during the winter or in hot, dry climates. Think about popping a small humidifier in your workspace or wherever you spend the most time.

It might seem like a quick fix to lick your lips to keep them moist, but that can make things worse. Saliva evaporates quickly, leaving a sticky residue that can attract bacteria and lead to infection. So, keep your tongue away from your lips and remember this: “Licking your lips will cause them to lickety-split.”

Whether from frigid cold or dry heat, your skin can lose water rapidly, causing cracking, flaking, discoloration, or swelling. So avoid jumping from a sweltering afternoon at the beach into a freezing cold movie theater.

Also, skip the hot showers or cold plunges for a bit. These types of rapid temperature changes will quickly dry out your lip corners. Bonus tip: Your lips can take a beating from the sun, so find a lip balm with SPF protection.

If your cracked lip corners don’t improve or become especially painful or swollen in a few days, it’s time to visit a board-certified dermatologist. If left untreated, angular cheilitis can last for years, leaving your lips discolored or scarred.

FYI: Angular cheilitis might not appear as clearly in people with darker skin. Instead of turning red, the affected skin may look pale and have a darker border.

Remember that lickety-split mantra? It’s for real. Saliva can get deposited in the corners of your lips for many reasons, like drooling, smoking, or sleeping with your mouth open due to some sniffles. Bacteria grows in those little saliva pools, triggering an inflammatory response that causes your lip corners to get irritated and crack.

Following these tips will make your lips feel better in about a week. Really bad cases of angular cheilitis can take a few weeks. Avoid smoking and eat a balanced diet to get faster results.

As mentioned above, Vaseline and other occlusives help create a protective barrier over the cracked lip corners, which helps the healing process.

You might have woken up with cracked lip corners, but you won’t be able to get rid of them overnight. Be patient and follow the tips above!

Say goodbye to painful cracked lip corners in about a week with these easy tips:

Talk to a dermatologist for customized care if your lip corners become red, swollen, or more painful after a few days.

#8984. Meet Lanza Atelier, Frida Escobedo's pick for the most influential architect of the next 20 years

They started the year crowned the 2026 Serpentine Pavilion architects and are ending it as trailblazer Frida Escobedo‘s pick for the practitioners who will shape the next two decades.

In this interview for Dezeen’s 20×20 series sponsored by Kohler, Lanza Atelier discuss the bathrooms that brought them together, the yin and yang of their partnership, and their hopes for the future.

The 20×20 series, launched to mark 20 years of Dezeen, is a two-stage affair: first, we rounded up 20 designers and architects who we’ve seen make a major impact over those 20 years, then we asked them to nominate the emerging practitioners that they think will make a big impact on the next 20.

With just 10 years between the start of their practices, Escobedo and Lanza Atelier represent two crests on a new wave of Mexican architecture that has brought regional references to the world stage and made adventurous but sympathetic interventions at home in Mexico City.

Escobedo was one of Lanza Atelier’s Alessandro Arienzo’s teachers at the Universidad Iberoamericana in Mexico City, and he and partner Isabel Abascal cite her as an inspiration whose success with kindred ideas has given them the confidence to pursue their vision.

They are becoming known for distilling complexity down to simple and pure gestures, whether in the appropriately snaking crinkle-crankle walls of their Serpentine Pavilion, inspired by the English countryside, their Cancun house with materials and forms drawn from sea snail shells, their Re-Source exhibition design that visitors could take home, or their hierarchy-challenging Family of 4 chairs, prompted by the arrival of their second son.

For Escobedo’s part, she identifies Arienzo and Abascal’s dedication to concept and process, which involves extensive research and testing, as key to their strength.

“Their work is poetic and intellectually rigorous,” said Escobedo. “They work seamlessly across scales, bringing together material intelligence, generosity, and a sense of play that makes their architecture both thoughtful and joyful.”

The Lanza story began in 2015, with toilets. Arienzo was approached by a client who, nearing the end of their bike path development in Mexico City, realised that they needed public bathroom facilities along the route. Arienzo suggested to Abascal, originally from Madrid, that they work on together on the project.

Their work is poetic and intellectually rigorous. They work seamlessly across scales, bringing together material intelligence, generosity, and a sense of play

Quickly, their collaboration turned one of architecture’s humblest structures into a nexus for meaning and care.

“We were exploring the scarcity of means and materials, but also the boundaries between inside and outside, and how to make something very simple like a toilet become something larger, like a meeting point and a resting space,” said Abascal.

“And also how to plan for the future of public architecture that might not be very taken care of or maintained by combining landscape and construction.”

The finished project features semi-open structures built from concrete blocks and filled with planting, creating a network of shaded resting points along the exposed track.

From the very first project we did together, we needed to arrive at something that was not Alessandro nor me, but Lanza. Our process has been so similar, in a way [ever since]

Bamboo trees loosely divide the male and female toilets, but they share common sinks – a feature that Lanza Atelier pushed for as part of their vision for a space of respectful coexistence between all users.

“It came out really naturally and fun, and simple,” said Arienzo. “That first interaction made Lanza happen because we needed to build a company after that.”

The nature of the collaboration pushed them to establish a distinct language from the get-go, adds Abascal.

“From the very first project we did together, we needed to arrive at something that was not Alessandro nor me, but Lanza,” she said.

“Our process has been so similar, in a way [ever since]. We explored so many different options, and we were so opinionated about how it should be. We very rigorously really gave all the importance to designing a toilet.”

As Escobedo identifies, Lanza Atelier’s work has a remarkable sense of play considering it lacks the colour, ornamentation or usual curlicues that would prompt association with the word.

Their use of materials is almost austere, in the sense that many of their projects have seen them hone in on just one material and push it to its limits, as in the local Sienna bricks of their Serpentine Pavilion.

Arienzo characterises this “extreme” approach as being “maybe a phase” more than a signature of the studio’s work. Instead, the key feature is how they arrive at the choice.

“We pick materials because of where the project is or what we have close to the site,” Arienzo said. “We analyse what’s the best or least aggressive way to build [in that place], because, we always say, building is really violent.”

Using fewer materials also allows them to focus more on questions of space, and makes it easier for their pavilions and installations, often demountable as a matter of principle, to find a second life.

“The main issue is achieving a degree of simplicity, which is very hard to do, because you start with complexity, and then you have to make decisions and to clean and to extract,” said Abascal.

The main issue is achieving a degree of simplicity, which is very hard to do, because you start with complexity, and then you have to make decisions and to clean and to extract

That’s where the playfulness comes in, the designers identify, allowing them to dig into various elements, flip them, manipulate them and be curious about them.

“That, I think, is the playground,” adds Arienzo.

When asked what qualities each of the duo brings to the table that makes their work together so strong, Arienzo is initially flippant.

But when the duo finally answers seriously, their responses do seem to reveal something about the alchemy going on behind the scenes.

“I used to call Alessandro’s gaze towards the world ‘the laser eye’,” said Abascal. “He is always pointing things out to me – mostly in our everyday lives, it’s things that the city creates and produces informally, but his laser eye applies to every context.”

“And it’s not only something visual but has to do with how things are and are put together and solved.”

For his part, Arienzo describes Abascal as the powerhouse behind Lanza’s ideas and concepts.

“I think she gives a lot of meaning to the projects,” said Arienzo. “I think without this, I would just do soulless stuff. She connects the work with history, with literature, with art.”

Lanza Atelier’s slate currently includes a house in LA to replace one destroyed by the wildfires, several projects in Mexico City and the design for the Expanded Tradition exhibition on contemporary Mexican craft at Qatari museum M7. When we speak, Abascal is on her way to the Canary Islands to conduct research on bird migration and pregnancy. It’s a patchwork that is idiosyncratically Lanza.

Neither Arienzo or Abascal seems to be the type to have a 10-year plan – asked about professional goals, Arienzo replies that they’re more orientated towards taking better care of themselves and their children – but they identify housing, particularly collective housing, as the type of architecture they most want to work on.

They hope to do it within a global industry that demolishes less and values what’s already built more, and that learns from the original “sustainable architecture” of vernacular construction in places like Mexico.

The country has been in the spotlight in the last few years as one of the few in Latin America with a progressive government, and one whose president, Claudia Sheinbaum, has frequently had to stand her ground against its northern neighbour.

Asked about whether government policy has had any positive effect on architecture and related industries at home, Abascal and Arienzo’s good cop and bad cop come out.

“From architects of the older generation, our generation and the younger generation, I can feel a sense of optimism,” said Abascal.

“I feel a sense of doing nothing,” said Arienzo. “Claudia is way better than what there was before; I’m a leftie. But I think there should be many more competitions around housing in the city.”

Both say they would like to see more public competitions in place of private developments, and that they would eagerly enter.

“Mexico City’s downtown is beautiful and it’s almost empty,” said Arienzo. “There isn’t a lot of density. I think it should be much more about that. Housing is a big issue and will be forever for these big cities.”

There is an ideal future for the architects, then. It’s one that would see the urban landscape of their home city benefit from the respect, creativity and serene beauty that is the Lanza calling card.

#8983. 5 Signs You’re in a One-Sided Friendship, According to Experts

Welcome to Asking for a Friend, a weekly series dedicated to solving the messy, awkward, and confusing parts of modern friendship. Because truth is, our platonic relationships are often the most complicated. Send us your friendship dilemmas here, and we might feature one in a future column.

Most friendships will never be truly 50/50, but at the very least they run on an unspoken agreement: both people show up, reach out, and add some fuel to the tank that keeps the engine going. If that balance consistently feels off—not just once or twice, but over the course of weeks or months—it’s hard not to wonder whether something deeper is going on.

You might notice in small but telling ways: Looking back at your messages, it dawns on you that you’re initiating every conversation. They call, if at all, only when they’re bored or when it’s convenient. And then there’s the sharper sting of noticing how effortlessly they find time for other people—just not for you (a surprisingly common frustration you can read more about here).

To be fair, life can get in the way—people get busy, schedules clash, and our friends can’t always be as available as we’d like—but that doesn’t make it any less frustrating or stop you from feeling resentful when you’re waiting days for a simple “How are you?” But how do you know if this is a temporary lapse or a more unhealthy one-sided friendship? Here are the biggest red flags therapists want you to watch out for.

Look through your texts and DMs: Are you always the first to send a message? When’s the last time they suggested hanging out? You can also experiment by not reaching out to see how long it takes for them to initiate contact. If weeks (or months) go by without a word, their silence may indicate who’s really holding this connection together.

“At a minimum, a good friend (even a busy one) will periodically check in out of curiosity and interest,” Tiana Leeds, LMFT, a therapist based in Santa Barbara, California, tells SELF. After all, someone who truly cares about you should want to know what’s going on in your life, which is why if they consistently don’t try to get in touch (or only expect you to do so), they may not be genuinely interested in your world.

Venting to your friends is natural—some would even argue it can strengthen your bond. That said, being there for each other is supposed to be a two-way street, Hope Kelaher, LCSW, author of Here to Make Friends: How to Make Friends as an Adult, tells SELF.

If someone unloads their laundry list of problems but doesn’t listen to yours, “they’re likely using you as their on-call therapist,” Kelaher says. This one-directional dynamic could look like a person who constantly complains about their boss but changes the subject whenever you open up about your work-related stress. Or they dominate dinner conversations with their dating disasters, yet they’re “busy,” uninterested, or MIA when you need relationship advice. Over time, investing all your time and energy into people who won’t give back can drain your energy, Leeds says, and leave you feeling neglected by a person who’s supposed to have your back.

Maybe they insist on eating at restaurants near their place, which means you have to travel across town every single time. They only reach out when “better” plans fall through (“Hey, my dinner got canceled. What are you doing tonight?”), making you feel more like an afterthought than a priority. More subtly, perhaps they’re only interested in brief 15-minute coffee chats that fit their schedule instead of a dedicated dinner or movie night.

“In a healthy relationship there should always be a give-and-take,” Kelaher says, meaning both people need to compromise. So it’s disheartening when, again and again, someone you’d do anything for won’t meet you halfway (sometimes literally).

Your friend might be a workaholic or chronically forgetful (which, don’t get us wrong, is still frustrating). But that alone doesn’t mean your bond is one-sided.

Instead, “consider the bigger picture and ask yourself, ‘Is their behavior a reflection of not caring about me, or just a difference in availability and communication style?’” Leeds says. As an example, someone who takes five business days to reply to anyone’s messages may not be singling you out. What’s more telling, though, is if that same person who’s “too swamped” to text you regularly posts Instagram stories of brunches, dinners, and post-work meetups with others in their social circle. Or if your usually punctual friend (who’s known for being reliable) is comfortable canceling plans only with you. These inconsistencies, Kelaher says, suggest that they’re perfectly capable of showing up—just not for you.

Let’s say you mentioned how important it would be to have support at your first 5K race. A friend who truly cares might surprise you at the finish line with flowers, or at the very least shoot over a heartfelt “Good luck!” or “Congrats!” In a one-sided friendship, however, this kind of consideration may be missing entirely. They might downplay your achievement (“Sorry I couldn’t make it, but it was such a short race!”) or forget your big day without a hint of apology.

True friends go the extra mile to celebrate your successes and be there during tough moments. That’s why if someone repeatedly forgets significant events like your birthday, or rarely shows empathy for your challenges (like a scary medical procedure, a high-stakes presentation), they may not be as invested as they should be.

Therapists recommended bringing up your concerns non-confrontationally.

Ideally, their response can give you a glimpse into whether they’re aware of this imbalance and, more importantly, if they’re willing to work on it. That said, you can’t force someone to be a good friend, so if they don’t care enough to show up for you, know that you deserve better. “After all, friendships take work, Leeds says. “But it’s not meant to be done by just one person.”

#8981. What Does Dark Green Poop Mean? Causes, Diet, and When to See a Doctor

Follow Greatist on our socials for all things health.

Bum nuggets typically sport a classic brown, so glancing back into the loo and spying on greenish-colored poop can throw you for a loop.

Most of the time, green poop reflects a leafy diet or your body’s unique way of breaking things down. But if the green becomes a recurring (fecal) matter, it might be something else.

Continue reading to learn more about poop color, its meaning, and when it’s time to make an appointment with a healthcare provider.

Spotting green or another unexpected color in the toilet can be startling, but it’s more common than you might think. From dietary influences to your body’s digestion speed, several factors can change poop from earthy tones to other shades. Let’s check some out.

Are you chowing down on lots of green leafy veggies like spinach, kale, or broccoli? These foods are high in chlorophyll, which can dye your doodles green. Chlorophyll doesn’t always break down entirely before reaching your intestines, meaning it passes through your system and colors your stool green.

Have you ever had a St. Paddy’s Day-themed milkshake or a brightly colored cake? Artificial colors in foods and drinks can change poop from brown to green. It’s not magic! It’s just the dye in green food passing through your gut unchanged.

When your digestive system processes food too rapidly, it doesn’t allow for the full breakdown of bile, a yellow-green fluid that aids digestion. This often results in a greenish stool, especially during fast-moving episodes of diarrhea.

Have you recently been taking antibiotics? These meds can reset your gut’s bacterial crew. Since these tiny critters play a big part in the shade of your stool, introducing antibiotics might cause green poop sometimes.

If you’ve had certain medical treatments, it can affect digestion and cause bright green poop. One example is graft-versus-host disease, which may occur with bone marrow transplants. This tricky condition can bring about less-than-welcome guests, like diarrhea and green stool. It’s a clear signal from your body that things are out of sync.

Some uninvited microscopic guests like Salmonella bacteria, the water-loving mini parasite Giardia, and norovirus can also be a reason for your poop turning green. These critters can hustle your digestion at an unnaturally quick pace, turning your stool green as they disrupt your gut’s usual rhythm.

Babies can surprise you with a whole crayon box of poop colors, and green is definitely in the mix.

For infants, green stool might stem from the same factors as adults, like dietary changes. This includes adjustments when they start eating solids or changes in a parent’s diet if chestfeeding.

Another harmless cause could be ingesting a small amount of amniotic fluid in the womb. So, if you notice your little one sporting some spring grass-colored diapers, it’s usually no biggie.

If the green theme park in your toilet isn’t closing down, or if it’s accompanied by other symptoms like severe stomach pain, nausea, or diarrhea, it might be time to call in the pros. Persistent changes in stool color may signal underlying health issues that need medical attention.

Dark green poop can result from eating lots of leafy greens or foods with green coloring. However, it can also indicate that food travels quickly through the digestive system.

While liver issues can change stool color, they usually turn it pale or dark, not green. If you’re worried about liver health, look for pale or clay-colored stools instead.

If you haven’t been on a kale-eating spree, dark green poop might be from iron supplements or constipation remedies, which can also give poop a greenish tint.

Dark poop could be a sign of your diet or medications. However, if it’s black and tar-like, it might mean bleeding in your upper gastrointestinal tract. In that case, chatting with a healthcare professional is a must.

While green poop can def throw you through a loop, it’s usually not a sign of anything serious. It’s often your body’s way of dealing with what you eat or how fast you digest. So, unless it’s paired with other worrying symptoms, there’s probably no need to panic.

#8980. CAN combines eclectic references for eccentric revamp of London house

Towers of concrete drainage tubes and colourful exposed steel elements are among the eclectic features of House Tropicália, a “very personal” London residence recently extended by local architecture studio CAN.

Located in Catford, the project responds to a brief with “two distinct strands” – one relating to the functional elements of the project, and the other to its expressive and atmospheric qualities.

Functionally, CAN was asked to introduce a new kitchen and dining space that felt connected to the garden, alongside two new bedrooms on the first floor.

Meanwhile, the design was required to be an expression of the interests and experiences of its clients – designer Fabiane Lee-Perrella, television producer Robin Lee-Perrella and their two sons.

“The atmospheric side of the brief was to somehow encapsulate the clients’ diverse visual tastes and architectural memories from their pasts,” CAN founder Mat Barnes told Dezeen.

“This resulted in the eclecticism of the project; one that is very personal to the clients.”

Visual references given to CAN included modernist Brazilian architecture projects such as Lina Bo Bardi’s SESC Pompéia in São Paulo, as well as industrial architecture, David Hockney paintings and Moroccan riads.

The resultant design inspired the project’s name, House Tropicália, which nods to the late 1960s Tropicália movement that celebrated bold ideas and rebelled against accepted norms.

“We reject the idea that a project needs to be driven by a single, homogeneous idea or material,” said Barnes.

“Instead, we celebrate the complexity, diversity and even contradiction inherent in our clients’ tastes and design references,” he continued.

“We see these different influences not as competing ideas, but as an opportunity to create something individual and ultimately more meaningful.”

The focal point of the project is its highly unique rear elevation, with features including two towers of engineering drainage tubes, which break through a red-steel canopy that extends over the patio.

Meanwhile, bright blue and red fibre-cement panels decorate its elevation, alongside portions of textured raked render and exposed concrete, punctured by irregular shapes.

Details also include a metal sawtooth roof at first-floor level, alongside a bright yellow screen facing the neighbouring property to prevent overlooking.

Finally, at ground level, a full-width set of doors open onto a patio with a winding perimeter, referencing the designs of Brazilian landscape architect Roberto Burle Marx.

“It brings together a mix of materials, forms and ideas drawn from the huge range of references the clients shared with us,” said Barnes. “I think it captures the character and personalities of the clients brilliantly.”

Inside, the back half of the ground floor has been rearranged to maximise its connection to the rear garden. This is where the new open-plan kitchen, dining and living space is positioned.

Meanwhile, at the front of the ground floor, the studio has created a secondary dining area and living space, and a children’s playroom in the original lounge.

Above, a void on the north side of the first floor has been filled to add a main bedroom suite, complete with an ensuite and roof terrace. Another bedroom has also been added.

The roof terrace has a walk-on, diamond-shaped skylight, which sits directly above the dining table.

Interior finishes echo the eclecticism of the exterior, with a bold mix of colours, materials and textures. This includes exposed steel joists and trusses, and a colourful timber kitchen with contrasting black tiles.

Walls of ceramic tiles on the ground floor have shell-like forms, handmade by Fabiane Lee-Perrella with glazing that shifts from pink to blue hues.

A microcement floor runs throughout the ground floor and incorporates pebble inlay that evokes a river and is a nod to the water feature at SESC Pompéia.

CAN hopes the project will highlight the importance of challenging the “established or standard way of doing things in a particular city or context”.

“We think it’s important to look beyond the usual architectural references and draw inspiration from unexpected places, whether that be sculpture, set design, or even infrastructure,” Barnes said.

“These disciplines can offer entirely different ways of thinking about space, material and form. Ultimately, it’s about exposing clients to these different ways of doing things.”

CAN, known fully as Critical Architecture Network, was founded by Barnes in 2016. Its previous projects include the equally bold house extensions Druid Grove and Mountain View.

#8979. Yes, Your Feet Age. Dermal Fillers Can Help

Barefoot walks on the beach. A day in their favorite high heels. A long training walk ahead of the Camano de Santiago. These are the goals—big and small—of women undergoing foot filler treatments.

Using an injectable filler—such as hyaluronic acid or body fat—to add padding to sore feet is not new, though it is gaining in popularity. As early as the 1960s, medical-grade silicone has been used to puff up padding deflated by age, years of wear and tear, and fashionable footwear, especially high heels. All of this puts intense pressure on the balls of the feet—otherwise known as the metatarsals.

Over time, the fatty cushion on the bottom of your feet dissipates. Fat pad atrophy affects 30% of people over the age of 60. Without that natural cushion, the bones in your feet come into closer contact with the ground, which causes a deep bruise-like pain in the heels or balls of the feet when walking barefoot or standing for long periods.

For some perspective, look at the doughy wonders that are baby feet and compare them to yours. As we age, wear and tear breaks down that plush tissue. And if you put your feet to heavy use, you’ll wear down that cushion quicker. Some of that internal cushioning can be restored—even if just temporarily—with the injection of dermal fillers.

“It’s getting very popular because people are already familiar with it for aesthetic [uses],” says Ben Pearl, DPM, a podiatrist at Arlington Foot and Ankle in Arlington, Virginia. Dr. Pearl specializes in sports medicine and treats endurance athletes looking to restore cushion lost in their feet from pounding the pavement.

Patients don’t have just one choice for injectables, though. Many of the same options available for cosmetic use have also shown promise for feet. There’s hyaluronic acid filler, which adds physical volume and cushioning, and calcium hydroxylapatite, such as Radiesse, which adds firm volume while also promoting new collagen growth. Sometimes human body fat is used as the injectable, known as adipose tissue, a practice that is quickly becoming the preferred method.

“[A fat injection] actually recruits your body to rebuild the fat pad in that area so it has a much longer duration,” says Anne Sharkey, DPM, of Soley Podiatry in Austin. Fat allografts from brands like Liposana and Leneva may last as long as two years, compared to hyaluronic acid fillers, which typically need a touch up in six to nine months.

This type of regenerative medicine is appealing to patients. It’s not a promise that the foot will return to its former glory, but that it will be “as close to normal as possible,” says Dr. Pearl.

Dr. Sharkey and Dr. Pearl have both seen positive results from their patients. Scientific studies corroborate the efficacy of the treatment as well. One small study looking at patients with metatarsal pain found five patients had no more pain six months post-hyaluronic acid injections, and those who still had pain could wear high heels twice as long as they could before the injections. Another study surveying patients who had been injected with body fat reported that their pain improved by more than 70 percent on average, 20 months post injection.

While there are a growing number of cosmetic clinics offering the procedure, Dr. Pearl cautions against allowing just any injector at it. That’s because injecting filler into feet is a more complex procedure than an aesthetic injection. For one, knowing where to inject requires an understanding of the foot’s pressure points. In his own practice, Dr. Pearl uses ultrasound to help determine where to replace the fat to offload the pain. Additionally, Dr. Pearl notes, the skin is much tougher on the feet than the face, making it a more complicated area to inject.

This is one reason why Dr. Sharkey set up her practice to include a nail salon—combining cosmetology and podiatry. Her patients are already familiar with dermal fillers. Within the attached nail salon you can get manicures, pedicures, ingrown nail treatment, toenail reconstruction, or dermal fillers for feet.

Try not to groan, but it depends. The cost of the procedure is influenced by how much filler is injected, and which brand is used. Other factors that affect cost include how your provider bills the procedure, and how much experience they have with dermal filler injections.

For cosmetic use, the American Society of Plastic Surgeons places the average cost of hyaluronic acid filler treatment at $715. They estimate nonhyaluronic acid fillers, including Radiesse, Sculptra, and Liposana to cost $901 on average per treatment. However, the feet will almost certainly require more filler than the face, so you can expect the cost to be higher.

But will insurance cover it? Unlikely. “Even though it isn't technically cosmetic, it may not be considered medically necessary, because these procedures are often considered elective and cosmetic branding has a box drawn around it,” says Mark Welter, chief strategy and growth officer at Welter Healthcare Partners, a healthcare business management firm.

If you’re transparent with your provider about any financial concerns you have, they can work with you to find a middle ground between pain relief and high costs. Dr. Sharkey, for example, will often offer her patients more affordable hyaluronic acid fillers as temporary pain relief until they’re ready to dive into a more expensive fat injection.

If injectables aren’t accessible to you, there are other ways to deal with foot pain. Here are some options, most of which require a low financial investment.

A podiatrist can help walk you through any of these options and come up with a plan to minimize your pain.

#8977. Atelier Manferdini uses digital glitches to shape tile-and-metal facade of Virginia power station

Photography by Dave Huh unless stated

California-based studio Atelier Manferdini has created an expressive facade system for an electrical substation in Virginia, USA, using metal and colourful tile to represent the flow of electrical power within.

Called InVisible, the project was carried out for Dominion Energy, an electricity provider that was updating the substation in Crystal City, Northern Virginia, just outside of Washington DC.

Atelier Manferdini founder Elena Manferdini, who is Italian and teaches at Sci-Arc in Los Angeles, said that her studio sought to translate the largely functional structure into something more human.

“Critical infrastructure is essential to our cities, yet the Dominion Energy substation is fundamentally designed for machines rather than people,” Manferdini told Dezeen.

“With inVisible, we wanted to explore this dichotomy, transforming a purely functional structure into something meaningful to the surrounding community,” she continued.

“While the interior responds to the needs of machines, the exterior becomes an opportunity to engage with people through color, pattern, and perception, creating a dialogue between infrastructure and the human scale of the city.”

The substation converts power into different voltages to facilitate the transmission of energy, and the patterns on the sculptural facade were computationally designed to represent that process.

Atelier Manferdini used programming site Processing, which came out of the MIT Media Lab in the early 2000s, to design the colourful tile band that lines the bottom of the structure.

This pattern incorporates 10 colours and tiles of three different sizes, two, four, and six inches across – a reference to voltages – along with “glitches” in the program to create the graphic.

It recalls the Boogie Woogie works of modernist artist Piet Mondrian, which were based on the rhythms of cities.

Above the ceramic pattern, the studio placed massive gridded aluminium panels.

The panels create a ventilated facade system, set at different distances from the exterior walls and stacked where they meet so that sunlight passes through different densities in the gridded pattern, creating a variable light effect.

“The folds catch light and cast shadows, allowing the surface to shift with the time of day and the viewer’s position,” said the studio.

At night, the panels are backlit by programmable LEDs.

Overall, the studio said that it considers the contrast between the monochromatic metal and colour tile patterns a unified image.

“Quiet and metallic above, saturated and granular below, the two bands form a unified architectural composition,” said the studio, with the unseen machines humming with electricity inside.

Other creative takes on infrastructure include a power station in China that Schmidt Hammer Lassen shrouded with steel lamellas and topped with a walkway, as well as a sculptural stormwater facility in Toronto by GH3, a Canadian studio well known for its aesthetic treatment of otherwise overlooked infrastructure.

#8975. What Is ‘Fiber Training’—And Why Should You Be Doing It?

With the fibermaxxing fad encouraging people to prioritize this chronically neglected nutrient, one issue keeps coming up: the side effects. As important as hitting your daily fiber goal is, your body doesn’t always make doing so easy. Fiber is difficult for your digestive system to break down and has to be handed off to bacteria in the colon instead (which is kind of its point), so piling on too much too fast can result in a barrage of painful, awkward, or inconvenient digestive symptoms—bloating, gas, stomach cramps, the whole nine yards.

To be clear, GI distress isn’t a sign to abandon your pursuit of a higher-fiber diet. “Even with fiber becoming a growing trend, people still greatly underestimate its importance and, also, just how many ways it benefits the human body,” Desiree Nielsen, RD, a recipe developer with a focus on plant-based nutrition, tells SELF. You’re probably familiar with fiber’s ability to keep you full, stave off constipation, and support gut health, but it wears plenty of other hats too, like lowering “bad” LDL cholesterol and stabilizing your blood sugar (not to mention reducing your risk for a slew of diseases in the long run). In fact, overlooking fiber is one of the top nutrition mistakes people make, according to experts.

But if you feel apprehensive at the thought of fighting constant stomach discomfort in the process of working to correct a fiber deficiency, we don’t blame you. In fact, it’s a complaint that Lisa Ganjhu, DO, a gastroenterologist at NYU Langone Health, hears all the time at work: “I have a lot of patients that will say ‘I ate more fiber, and now I’m really bloated and crampy,’” she says. Thankfully, there’s a way to curtail those disagreeable side effects so you can (comfortably) continue your fiber journey: a strategy Nielsen calls fiber training. Here’s what that involves, and how to start developing those “muscles.”

Fiber training is exactly what it sounds like: training your body to handle fiber better. It’s all about “slow, consistent increases in fiber to help you build your tolerance…while minimizing the potential symptoms,” Nielsen says.

You can think of fiber training kind of like preparing for a race. “In much the same way that you wouldn’t go out and run a marathon tomorrow if you haven’t run a mile before,” you need to work your way up to a high-fiber diet, Nielsen says. Similarly, Dr. Ganjhu compares it to a weightlifting regimen. Rather than lifting 50-pound weights right off the bat, “you kind of have to adjust slowly,” she says. “You start off with 10. When that becomes easy, you go to 20, then you go to 30”—and so on.

Fiber training is especially critical if you’re constipated at the outset, as many people are, according to Nielsen. Even though fiber can help prevent and alleviate constipation, too much at once can actually make an existing issue worse by overwhelming your gut. “When you add a ton of fiber to an already backed-up system, it’s kind of like a bottleneck on the highway,” Nielsen says: If you try to shoehorn four lanes into one, you’re going to end up with a jam on your hands.

Now that you know fiber training entails steadily increasing your fiber intake, you’re probably wondering what that looks like on a more practical level. Before we share specifics, some context for how much fiber you actually need might be helpful. Per the federal Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2020-2025, women should aim for 28 grams of fiber daily from ages 19 to 30, 25 grams of fiber daily from ages 31 to 50, and 22 grams of fiber daily starting at age 51, though some experts recommend even more—a helpful set of parameters if you’re not sure where to start.

While the ideal amount of fiber to add to your diet while fiber training can vary from person to person depending on health needs (like a constipation issue), most people are “looking at [adding] probably three to five grams at a time,” Nielsen says.

With that in mind, you’ll want to choose a food that has a fiber content in that ballpark—say, an apple (around four grams of fiber), a half-cup of chickpeas (around five grams of fiber), a tablespoon of chia seeds (around five grams of fiber), or two tablespoons of ground flax (around four grams of fiber)—and eat a serving every single day until you feel like your body has adjusted (read: you’re not experiencing any additional bloating, gas, or other GI side effects). This process typically takes around five to seven days, according to Nielsen, but everyone’s digestive system is different, so don’t worry if you need more (or less!) time. “It really is about listening to your body and individualizing the rate at which you increase,” Nielsen says. “You have to follow your symptoms and go slow,” Dr. Ganjhu agrees.

Then, you can tack on another dose—like a second apple, a full cup of chickpeas, two tablespoons of chia seeds, or four tablespoons of ground flax. Continue increasing your fiber intake in these increments (and at this pace) until you’ve hit your daily fiber goal. If you’re a 35-year-old woman starting from scratch, reaching 25 grams of fiber—the recommended daily amount for that age—would take around five five-gram doses, six four-gram doses, or eight three-gram doses, for example.

People who are constipated may want to specifically fiber train with foods that are low in FODMAPs—fermentable carbohydrates particularly hard on sensitive stomachs—according to Nielsen. Like we said above, increasing your fiber intake when you’re backed up can, well, backfire, so low-FODMAP foods are more likely to be a safe bet than their high-FODMAP counterparts. Kiwis, which contain four grams of fiber in a two-fruit serving, are an especially strong option if you fall into this category (and they’ve even been specifically studied as a dietary constipation treatment), Nielsen says. Similarly, she adds, a gentle fiber supplement like Metamucil, which is made from psyllium husk, also “provides a lot of the benefits, but tends to be less irritating to a troubled system.”

Another tip: If you’re constipated, make sure to drink plenty of water as well (though the oft-referenced eight-glasses-a-day requirement is something of a myth!). Because fiber needs water to work its stool-softening magic, insufficient fluids could leave your bowel movements hard and dry, exacerbating the problem.

Whatever new fiber sources you choose, taking this slow-and-steady approach should help ease the transition to a higher intake. “If you’re someone who doesn’t eat a lot of fiber and all of a sudden you start eating 30 grams of it, the colon is just not going to know how to manage that efficiently,” Dr. Ganjhu says. But by leveling up little by little? You can heighten that “colonic fitness”—and sidestep the worst of the awkward stage.

#8972. How to Calculate Your Rising and Moon Sign: A Beginner’s Guide

Follow Greatist on our socials for all things health.

The sun sign is the *it girlie* of the “big three” elements in astrology.

But do you know about your moon sign and rising sign?

We chatted with an astrologer to understand what they are and how to calculate them.

According to Olga Verkhotina — astrologer and personal coach — the big three in astrology are your three most significant chart elements:

“While a natal chart contains so many more intricate details beyond just three elements, the big three is a way to determine the main highlights that make up your personality and overall temperament,” Verkhotina says.

Verkhotina explains that a rising sign is the zodiac sign that falls at the beginning of your First House — basically, the beginning of your natal chart.

“The First House in astrology is associated with a person’s identity, individual activity, even their appearance, and the sign that houses that theme gives its characteristics,” she says.

“Knowing your rising sign describes the way others may perceive you, the way your behavior comes across, as well as how you approach new situations in life.”

You’ll need: date, time and place of birth.

“Knowing the accurate time is important here because even 10 minutes can make a difference in the sign,” Verkhotina explains.

“Once you have the data, you can trust astrology software to calculate it for you. There are a lot of natal chart calculators online, so you can just search ‘rising sign calculator,'” Verkhotina says.

Pro tip: Verkhotina suggests reading horoscopes from your rising sign instead of your sun sign, saying it will likely give more personalized insights on which areas of your life might be impacted by current cosmic events.

“A moon sign describes the position of the moon on the zodiac wheel at the moment of your birth,” Verkhotina says.

She explains that the moon in astrology symbolizes:

“The moon sign helps you better understand how these themes demonstrate themselves in your life,” Verkhotina says.

Unlike the rising sign, you don’t have to have the precise time of birth to know your moon sign, although Verkhotina says it’s still recommended.

You can also use an online calculator to find your moon sign or refer to the ephemeris — a table showing the daily positions of planets.

Verkhotina describes the sun sign as the most important planet in your chart.

“It’s the center of your vitality, your ego, consciousness, and individuality at its core. That’s why it’s the most commonly known element in astrology,” she says.

It represents the zodiac sign the sun was in at the time of your birth, which Verkhotina says gives your individuality certain qualities associated with its specific sign.

“It’s important to understand that although the sun is a huge element in astrology, it doesn’t cover the nuances of one’s character,” Verkhotina explains.

Instead, she says it just represents overall traits.

Verkhotina adds that the specifics of your character are covered in the rest of your astrological chart. “This is why sometimes no two leos are the same,” she says.

This one is easy peasy — you don’t have to have your time or place of birth.

“The sun cycle is very similar every year, so you can look it up by the date, month and year of your birth. Each sign corresponds to a calendar date that year,” Verkhotina says.

Here’s each astro sign, in a nutshell, according to Verkhotina.

Your sun sign is important, but your moon and rising signs add extra details.

Your rising sign reflects your identity and how others see you, while your moon sign reveals your emotions and behavior.

To find these signs, you can use online birth chart calculators. Just make sure you have your birth date and time handy for accurate results.

Last medically reviewed on August 2, 2024
